map.不会改变切点本身，但切点在不同单位下的数值必须成套使用：空腹 ≥7.0 mmol: It does not change the cutoff itself, but the numeric cutoffs must be used as a consistent set across units: fasting >=7.0 mmol/L equals >=126 mg/dL, and 2-hour postprandial >=11.1 mmol/L equals >=200 mg/dL. Never treat 7.0 mmol/L as 70 mg/dL (that is actually 3.9 mmol/L, already in the hypoglycemic range); this kind of unit mismatch is one of the most dangerous misreadings in home monitoring.

map.差别在系数精度：取 18 得 100.8，取 18.0159 得 100.9。临: The difference is the precision of the factor: 18 gives 100.8 while 18.0159 gives 100.9. Clinical interpretation is unaffected (1 mg/dL is far below the allowed glucometer error, and ISO 15197 requires ±15% or ±15 mg/dL), but when checking digit by digit against a lab report use the precise factor 18.0159.
map.核对血糖仪（多为 mg/dL）与医院生化报告（多为 mmol/L）是否一致，避免: Check that the glucometer (mostly mg/dL) agrees with the hospital lab report (mostly mmol/L) to avoid a unit mix-up causing a dosing error.

map.：空腹血糖 5.6 mmol/L → 5.6 × 18.0159 ≈ 100.9: : fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L -> 5.6 x 18.0159 ≈ 100.9 mg/dL, which is in the normal range (3.9-6.1 mmol/L / 70-110 mg/dL). Random glucose 11.1 mmol/L -> x 18.0159 ≈ 200.0 mg/dL, reaching the random threshold for a diabetes diagnosis. In reverse, a meter showing 100.9 mg/dL -> / 18.0159 ≈ 5.60 mmol/L. Note that this tool implements "output value = input value x source unit factor / target unit factor" while the option factors are mmol/L = 1 and mg/dL = 18, so to get mmol/L -> mg/dL you must set "from" to mg/dL(18) and "to" to mmol/L(1) (5.6 x 18 / 1 = 100.8); the semantics of the selector are counter-intuitive, so check the magnitude of the output to verify the unit (mmol/L is single digits, mg/dL is in the hundreds). The blood glucose converter embedded in the site's "Medical Health Calculators" uses the precise 18.0159 (5.6 -> 100.9) and is preferable.
map.：葡萄糖分子量约 180.159，因此 1 mmol/L = 18.0159 m: : the molar mass of glucose is about 180.159, so 1 mmol/L = 18.0159 mg/dL (engineering practice often uses 18). mmol/L to mg/dL: mg/dL = mmol/L x 18.0159; mg/dL to mmol/L: mmol/L = mg/dL / 18.0159. Common correspondences: 3.9 mmol/L ≈ 70 mg/dL (lower limit of normal and the hypoglycemia alert), 5.6 ≈ 100.9, 6.1 ≈ 110 (upper limit of normal fasting), 7.0 ≈ 126.1 (fasting diagnostic threshold for diabetes), 7.8 ≈ 140 (upper limit of normal 2-hour postprandial), 11.1 ≈ 200.0 (symptomatic plus random diagnostic threshold).
